newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Central bank fixes bank borrowing for Pakistan.
newsitem.headline: Central bank fixes bank borrowing for Pakistan.

text.p: The State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) on Wednesday fixed the total government borrowing for budgetary support in fiscal 1997/98 (July-June) at 58 billion rupees, a bank statement said.
It said the decision was taken at the bank's central board of directors meeting in Peshawar where the credit plan for 1997/98 was approved.

"The main elements of the credit plan for 1997/98 are containment of monetary expansion to about 14 percent and of government borrowing for budgetary support from the SBP to 30 billion and that from commercial banks to 28 billion," it said.

The SBP also approved credit requirements of the private sector at 82 billion rupees for 1997/98 that would help revival of industrial activity in the private sector and an expected expansion in trade, the statement said.

"To finance the above volume of private sector credit, and to help banks reduce their mark-up rates on lending to the private sector, the board also decided to lower the statutory liquidity requirement by five percentage points to 20 percent."
Domestic bank borrowing may exceed 100 billion rupees in 1996/97 against an original target of 29.7 billion rupees, said a private bank executive, who asked not to be named.
